key_source.why_it_had_to_move: R1 (bare V), R2 (particle surname) and R3 (glued annotation) are functions of the RAW string. payroll_payee_key deletes the V, splits the particle surname and absorbs the annotation before the triple exists, so no function of the triple can express them.
key_source.how_this_report_reaches_the_raw: the v6 spine and spans carry no payee_raw, so the three bound payroll corpora are re-keyed with the builder's own payroll_payee_key and joined on the triple

cause_vocabulary.ascii_punct: the fold to [a-z0-9] alone moves the key
cause_vocabulary.suffix: lifting a separator-delimited suffix out of the surname moves it further
cause_vocabulary.nickname_class: folding the given name onto its class stem
cause_vocabulary.v_initial: R1 -- a bare V the builder deleted is now the middle initial and reaches the key
cause_vocabulary.particle_surname: R2 -- a ruled particle joins the surname, so last grows and first/mi shift
cause_vocabulary.annotation_strip: R3 -- a glued job title leaves the surname, or a trailing party word stops supplying a phantom middle initial
cause_vocabulary.first_from_raw: the raw parse reads a different given name than the stored triple
cause_vocabulary.other: the key moved and none of the above explains it

ambiguity.note: a triple whose raws disagree on the v1.1 key. The builder keys on ONE raw (the anchor node's first observation), which this report cannot see, so these people are the exact population on which a builder histogram may differ from this one.
ambiguity.resolution_rule: prefer a non-empty middle initial, then the most frequently recorded, then the lexicographic minimum

cooccurrence_guard_preview.note: PREVIEW of the ruled guard 'two legacy ids that ever appear as distinct payee lines in the same report period AND office are NOT merged'. A v6 span row carries first_period, last_period and an OBSERVATION COUNT -- not the list of periods observed -- so this report can only test whether two spans share an office and OVERLAPPING period windows. That is an UPPER BOUND on the ruled condition in general. It is EXACT for every pair listed below, because each overlap collapses to a single period ordinal (start == end), which is the same report period.
cooccurrence_guard_preview.consequence: every merge group on this generation is blocked, so the guard makes the merge feature inert on the current data: spine_persons would stay at the baseline count and merge_ids_removed would be 0

name_key_collisions_ignoring_the_anchor.note: distinct spine ids sharing one name key, ignoring the office anchor -- what a name-only join collides on

splits.why_zero_is_expected: the v1.1 key is resolved per TRIPLE and a spine person carries exactly one triple, so the map stays many-to-one and a split is structurally impossible; it is verified, not asserted

anchor_reconstruction.method: min over office spans of (period start ordinal, chamber, office_key); id re-digested over {chamber, first_office_key, first_period, payee_key}
